forecasts.reason: Theory: the finish readout sits in each matrix's top direction and its size sets finishing. RL-Code's top-8 at 1x also carries the Okay/Wait readout but at smaller singular values than Math's (Code top-8 gave 178 vs Math's 192 on hard328). So the cell lands below Math top-8 plain (about 432/500 = 86%) at about 74%, i.e. 185 of 250.

Theory: finishing is set by the size of the top direction. At 0.125x of the full difference that size is small, so the model stays nearer plain base (224) than theta 0.25 (405, which bf16 rounding may already shrink to about 0.12); wide interval because rounding is uncertain.
Theory: 1.5x per direction is below the 2x over-commit point, so no breakdown and the stored 184 should hold. Expect regression toward the mean over 4 samples (seed spread about ±9).
Theory: 1.5x per direction is below 2x, so no over-commit or breakdown and the band keeps its stored level (183). Mean of 2 samples, slight regression.
Theory: 1.5x per direction is below 2x, so the late band keeps its stored 166, which is near base and random (late layers add no right answers). Mean of 2 samples.

Theory: commit-and-stop sits mainly in the top direction. Dropping it from the L0-10 edit (184 right, 98 cap hits) removes its finishing share, so right answers fall toward base and random (159-164) and cap hits stay high.
Theory: only the RL top direction's size moves finishing, so a random rank-8 edit does nothing. Expect base and random levels (158-167 across sizes).
Theory: a negative top-direction size lowers finishing. On hard328, -1x raised cap hits from 77 to 96 (x1.25), so the cued base's 22-27 MATH-500 cap hits rise to about 35-40.

Theory: the top direction's size sets finishing, so top-8 at 1.5x acts on Think-SFT like a full transplant at a=1.5 in finishing terms. That is between a=1 (220) and a=2 (232), with fewer cap hits than Think-SFT's 209.

Theory: about 3x on the top direction breaks generation into word strings whether 1 or 8 directions are scaled (base top-8 at 3x: 117), so Think-SFT drops well below its 209. Wide because the full a=3 transplant kept 227.
Theory: a random rank-8 edit has no RL top-direction size, so it does not change finishing and Think-SFT stays at its single-sample level (about 209; noise control 209).
Theory: per-direction size, not the number of directions, sets finishing and breakdown. Math+Code at 1.5x each (nearly orthogonal) acts like the 1.5x Math edit (about 200), with no over-commit.
Theory: per-direction size 1x sets finishing as in the 1x Math edit (192/328). Adding Code's directions does not raise the per-direction size.
Theory: the random rank-8 adds no RL top-direction size, so the cell equals Math top-8 alone (192 at 1x, about 200 at 1.5x).
Theory: per-direction size 1.5x is below breakdown and code answers are short, so the pair acts like Code top-8 at 1.5x (399) and does not add up; slight cost from the extra Math perturbation.
Theory: per-direction size 1x sets finishing as in Code top-8 at 1x (386/538). The Math directions add no size.
Theory: random rank-8 adds nothing, so the cell equals Math top-8 on code (368 at 1.5x).

Theory: 2x over-commits on long problems, so M(2) finishes more wrong answers and its vote gain over its single mean (231.5) is smaller than Think-SFT's 32. Expect about +14, like RL's vote and M(2)'s fresh2026 vote gain.
Theory: 2x over-commit costs only on long problems, and MATH-500 answers are short. So M(2) sits at or slightly above a=1 (467) and Think-SFT singles (457-462).
Theory: at 2x, M(2) over-commits, so fewer of its answers are cut. The roughly 50 remaining cap hits finish at 32k with about a quarter right, which adds about 10 to the 231.5 seen at 16k.
Theory: 2x over-commits on long problems (on hard328, 2x gave 190 vs 203 at 1.5x). MATH-500 is mostly short, so the cost against the 1.5x cell's 456 is small.
